note: fact_capable is set ONLY when a runner-owned oracle re-drive exists AND the ToolSpec passes the conformance battery (live.conformance). Everything else is LEAD-only or excluded. The count that matters is fact_capable, not the upstream tool count. Two FACT families are VIGIL-DIRECT (no tool is the authority): VERSION_RANGE via live.sbom (SBOM/dependency-CVE) and ACHIEVED_STATE via live.web_redrive — both HEADER-DERIVED (3xx Location, CORS headers, OIDC via Location) and BODY-DERIVED evidence. An undeclared charset, brotli/zstd, concatenated members and truncated reads are INCONCLUSIVE, and no-channel is INCONCLUSIVE not CLEAN. Their proposer tools (trivy/grype, httpx) keep fact_capable=false by design.

tools.name: sslscan
tools.notes: PROPOSER ONLY: sslscan says where a TLS service is; its per-cipher rows are never evidence. The runner re-drives FOUR of its OWN bounded, scope-gated handshakes per endpoint and deterministic oracles judge those. FACT-capable branches: tls_weakness.tls_handshake (baseline modern-client negotiation), weak_crypto.cert_signature_algorithm (the presented leaf's signature hash), tls_weakness.deprecated_protocol_offer (VIGIL offers ONLY TLS1.0, then ONLY TLS1.1, and the endpoint completes the handshake), and tls_weakness.weak_cipher_offer (VIGIL offers ONLY a closed 29-name weak-suite vocabulary at exactly TLS1.2 - the version pinned at both ends so the oracle's fire is attributable to the CIPHER and not to a deprecated version - and the endpoint SELECTS one). NO sslscan branch is CLEAN-capable. tls_weakness.deprecated_protocol_offer was briefly declared so and was DEMOTED on review: a protocol refusal is now always INCONCLUSIVE. The reason is that the corroborating handshake and the refusal necessarily happen on two DIFFERENT TCP connections, and nothing in the retained evidence binds them to the same peer - an L4 pool (a k8s Service with several pods, an haproxy/nginx TCP pool, a VIP, a DNS A-record pool) can refuse TLS1.0 on one connection and accept it on the next, which a red-pen reproduced end to end. The refused leg presents no certificate, so the spki_sha256 the completed leg retains has nothing to bind against; the gap is irreducible with what TLS gives that leg, and repeating the probe would only make the claim probabilistic. All the guards remain and still run (the closed alert(70) reason set, the channel_established precondition, and the peer_tls_session witness that keeps a bare non-TLS alert emitter out of any conclusive path); they simply no longer reach CLEAN. See the registry row's blocking_work. Boundaries: weak_tls on the baseline handshake is scoped to what a modern client still negotiates; the weak-cipher branch is not clean-capable because the local OpenSSL build limits which legacy suites can be offered at all (11 of 29 here), so a refusal may mean untested, and its TLS1.2 floor means a TLS1.0/1.1-max endpoint is not weak-cipher tested by it; and tls_weakness.certificate_validity (expired / not-yet-valid / hostname mismatch / self-signed) is NOT WIRED - the derivation exists and is tested, but no OracleKind adjudicates certificate validity, so no re-drive admits to that branch and it produces nothing. See its registry row's wired:false and blocking_work.

tools.name: httpx
tools.notes: HexStrike W2 web-discovery LEAD ENRICHER (branch achieved_state.endpoint_liveness) -- NOT fact_capable. httpx PROPOSES URLs and VIGIL re-drives EACH with its OWN plain gated GETs: the target (resampled) plus TWO runner-built sibling cohorts -- randomized same-shape siblings for a SAME-STATUS baseline (off-branch rejects discarded, an in-branch unstable sibling fails the run closed, validator-aware for Luhn / base58 / UUIDv4) and minimal-edit-distance siblings as a NO-TWIN search. The capture is retained, re-verifies offline, and is attached as LEAD evidence (priority + context); it NEVER mints. DOWNGRADED PERMANENTLY after five adversarial rounds, each of which found a NEW class of url where NOTHING EXISTS and the predicate minted a signed, offline-re-verifying FACT. The two that decided it: per-position FORMAT routes (^report\d$ / ^user\d{3}$ / ^dashboard\d$) measured 11/100, 32/100 and 55/100 direct plus 29-40/80 through both runner legs, because the sibling cohorts draw every alphanumeric position from a PER-SEGMENT UNION alphabet -- they do NOT mirror the target's EXACT per-position class (only the non-alnum separators are per-position), so a Hamming-1 edit at a digit slot becomes a letter ~74% of the time and the route rejects it; and a SKEWED per-PATH bounded not-found body space measured 13/100 direct, 9/80 httpx, 13/80 ffuf. On one route where /o/dashboard9 EXISTS and /o/dashboard1 does not, it minted 40/40 for the existing id and 21/40 for the nonexistent one -- it barely discriminates. Every earlier 'EXACT per-position class', 'the local-constraint family is CLOSED at 0/80', 'the residual is a whole-string checksum' and 'bounded not-found body space measured at 0' note is WITHDRAWN; the corrected statements and the retention-completeness trust boundary are in docs/capability-matrix/evidence-branches.json, which governs admission. The tool's row was never the fact authority and is not one now. HTTP exposure is re-derived by VIGIL's live.web_redrive ACHIEVED_STATE path (no install): VIGIL issues its OWN gated, no-redirect capture and the deterministic predicate_oracle adjudicates — the tool is only a URL proposer, never the fact authority (fact_capable stays false). CAPABILITY BOUNDARY (honest, narrower than the family name): HEADER-DERIVED evidence — a 3xx Location host, CORS reflected-origin-with-credentials, an OIDC redirect proven through Location — is both FACT- and CLEAN-capable. BODY-DERIVED branches (meta-refresh / body redirect, host-header reflected into HTML, the JS redirect sink) are FACT-capable but NOT CLEAN-capable. The decode gap that once made them unsound is CLOSED: integration/vigil_integration/live/body_decode.py reverses Content-Encoding (a complete, single-member, bounded gzip/deflate stream) and determines the charset the way a browser does (BOM, then the transport Content-Type label resolved through the WHATWG encoding map, strict decode), and body_semantically_available gates every body-dependent predicate — so an undeclared charset, a brotli/zstd body, concatenated members or a truncated read yield INCONCLUSIVE instead of a CLEAN over a document VIGIL never read. The JS-redirect branch mints only from EXECUTABLE code, decided by a real tokenizer (engine/crucible/framework/v2/scanner/js_lex.py:sink_is_executable — comments, string/template literals and ambiguous /-spans are excluded structurally), so it is FACT-capable rather than LEAD-only. What keeps the body branches from CLEAN is no longer decoding but ABSENCE: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the document declares no redirect' from 'we could not read this document', and lexing cannot prove a runtime-assembled sink absent (that needs DOM rendering, which is not wired). Per-branch limitations and blocking_work are in docs/capability-matrix/evidence-branches.json, which governs admission.
